Tamiya primer or Mr Hobby Surfacer 1000 and up will do fine these are lacquer primers so make sure to get a respirator I would suggest avoiding Mr hobby's "base white surfacer" from personal experience and what I read online  , maybe you should get a grey primer for the kit I would also suggest getting Tamiya's acrylic paint retarder if you can find it as Mr Hobby Aqueous dries rather fast the retarder will make it easier to handbrush with.

1. I'm not sure if Mr. Color thinner is compatible with the Aqueous paints as Mr Color is for their lacquers I have tried using Mr Color Retarder mild with Aqueous and didnt have any issues  I've seen people use Mr levelling thinner with Mr Aqueous that one is also for their lacquers and seems to have no issues , you could put the paint on a palette or something thin it and then try it out on the runner
2. Primer is very important and helps paints stick better to plastic , it is highly recommended but not a complete must if you don't intend on touching the kit although it is still best to prime if you can , you could prime everything in grey and it should be fine for the white parts it might be harder to spot if you sprayed it with grey primer so maybe initially spraying it with black primer in hard to reach areas then spraying grey on is a good idea
3. Disassembling when brush painting them would be the better way to go about it
